title: Unit 1: Key Vocabulary & Terminology (Part 1) 📚
content: 📌 Welcome Freshmen Students to Communicative English Skills I (EnLa101)! 👋✨ Here is the complete vocabulary list for Unit 1: Study Skills, formatted clearly for study and exam preparation. 1. Transient (Adjective) • English: Lasting for a very short time; temporary. • Amharic: ጊዜያዊ፣ አላፊ • Synonyms: Temporary, Fleeting • Antonyms: Permanent, Lasting • Example: Spoken language is transient, so taking notes during a lecture is essential. 2. Distractions (Noun) • English: Things that prevent someone from giving full attention. • Amharic: ትኩረት የሚስቡ/የሚያበላሹ ነገሮች • Synonyms: Interruptions, Disturbances • Antonyms: Focus, Concentration • Example: Sit near the front of the room to avoid environmental distractions. 3. Verbatim (Adverb / Adjective) • English: In exactly the same words as were used originally. • Amharic: ቃል በቃል • Synonyms: Word-for-word, Exactly • Antonyms: Paraphrased, Summarized • Example: Do not try to write down the lecture verbatim; focus on main ideas. 4. Cues (Noun) • English: Signals or hints given by a speaker to indicate key points. • Amharic: ጠቋሚ ምልክቶች • Synonyms: Signals, Hints, Indicators • Antonyms: Misdirections, Distractions • Example: Good students listen for vocal cues from the lecturer to identify important topics.

title: Unit 1: Key Vocabulary & Terminology (Part 2) 📖
content: 📌 5. Discriminating (Adjective) • English: Having or showing refined judgment; selective. • Amharic: መምረጥ የሚያውቅ፣ ለይቶ አዋቂ • Synonyms: Selective, Perceptive • Antonyms: Indiscriminate, Careless • Example: Effective note-taking requires being a discriminating listener. 6. Invaluable (Adjective) • English: Extremely useful; priceless. • Amharic: እጅግ ጠቃሚ፣ ዋጋ የማይተመንለት • Synonyms: Priceless, Crucial • Antonyms: Worthless, Useless • Example: Reading provides invaluable knowledge for your future career. 7. Skim (Verb) • English: Read quickly to get the general idea or gist. • Amharic: አጠቃላይ ሐሳቡን ለማግኘት በፍጥነት ማንበብ • Synonyms: Glance through, Scan roughly • Antonyms: Read thoroughly, Scrutinize • Example: I skimmed through the chapter to understand the main topic before class. 8. Scan (Verb) • English: Look through text quickly to locate a specific piece of information. • Amharic: የተወሰነ መረጃ/ቃል በፍጥነት መፈለግ • Synonyms: Search, Browse • Antonyms: Ignore, Overlook • Example: Scan the table of contents to find where the vocabulary section is located.

title: Unit 1: Key Vocabulary & Terminology (Part 3) 💡
content: 📌 9. Assimilate (Verb) • English: Take in and fully understand information or ideas. • Amharic: መቀበል፣ መረዳት፣ መዋሃድ • Synonyms: Absorb, Comprehend • Antonyms: Misunderstand, Reject • Example: Students read academic books to assimilate new concepts into their understanding. 10. Repertoire (Noun) • English: A stock of skills, techniques, or devices used in a particular field. • Amharic: የተካኑባቸው ክህሎቶች/ልምዶች ስብስብ • Synonyms: Collection, Stock, Range • Antonyms: Limitation, Inability • Example: University students should use their entire repertoire of reading skills. 11. Cursory (Adjective) • English: Hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed. • Amharic: ላዩን ብቻ የሆነ፣ ፈጣን ምልከታ • Synonyms: Superficial, Hasty • Antonyms: Thorough, Detailed • Example: A newspaper often gives only a cursory coverage of complex events. 12. At their disposal (Idiom / Phrase) • English: Available for one's use whenever desired. • Amharic: በእጃቸው ላይ ያለ፣ ለመጠቀም የተዘጋጀ • Synonyms: Available, Ready for use • Antonyms: Unavailable, Restricted • Example: Students have various learning strategies at their disposal.

title: Unit 1: Key Vocabulary & Terminology (Part 4) 🔑
content: 📌 13. Keys (Noun) • English: Essential tools or crucial factors that provide access to understanding. • Amharic: ዋና ቁልፎች፣ ወሳኝ መሳሪያዎች • Synonyms: Essentials, Secrets, Solutions • Antonyms: Obstacles, Barriers • Example: Reading skills are the keys to unlocking complex academic knowledge. 14. Access (Noun / Verb) • English: The opportunity or means to enter, approach, or retrieve information. • Amharic: ማግኘት፣ የመጠቀም ዕድል • Synonyms: Entry, Admission, Availability • Antonyms: Restriction, Limitation • Example: Students need easy access to diverse library reference materials. 15. Perceptions (Noun) • English: The ways in which something is regarded, understood, or interpreted. • Amharic: ግንዛቤዎች፣ አመለካከቶች • Synonyms: Views, Insights, Attitudes • Antonyms: Misunderstandings, Misconceptions • Example: Academic reading helps broaden a student's perceptions of world issues. 16. Interpreted (Verb) • English: Explained, understood, or analyzed in a specified way. • Amharic: ተተረጎመ፣ ትርጉም ተሰጠው • Synonyms: Understood, Analyzed, Clarified • Antonyms: Misconstrued, Misunderstood • Example: The survey results were interpreted using statistical analysis.

title: Unit 1: Key Vocabulary & Terminology (Part 5) 🎯
content: 📌 17. Glancing through (Phrasal Verb) • English: Looking at or reading something very quickly without paying attention to detail. • Amharic: ላዩን መመልከት፣ በፍጥነት ማየት • Synonyms: Browsing, Skimming, Flipping through • Antonyms: Studying, Scrutinizing • Example: He was glancing through the daily paper while waiting for the lecture. 18. Extract (Verb) • English: To remove, derive, or select specific facts or main points from a text. • Amharic: መቀነስ፣ መረጃ መዞር/ማውጣት • Synonyms: Obtain, Withdraw, Gather • Antonyms: Insert, Add • Example: Effective note-takers extract only the essential points from the presentation. 19. Vary (Verb) • English: To change or differ according to the circumstances or purpose. • Amharic: መለያየት፣ መለዋወጥ • Synonyms: Differ, Alter, Fluctuate • Antonyms: Remain constant, Stay same • Example: Your reading speed should vary based on the difficulty of the passage. 20. Themes (Noun) • English: The main ideas, subjects, or underlying topics in a text or lecture. • Amharic: ዋና ዋና ርዕሰ ጉዳዮች/ሀሳቦች • Synonyms: Topics, Subject matters, Core ideas • Antonyms: Details, Minor facts • Example: The professor outlined the central themes of the course during the orientation. 21. Recognizing (Verb) • English: Identifying or acknowledging words, concepts, or details previously learned. • Amharic: መለየት፣ ማወቅ • Synonyms: Identifying, Perceiving • Antonyms: Ignoring, Overlooking • Example: Reading is about understanding context, not just recognizing individual words. --- ❤️ Dear EthioFresh Students! All vocabulary terms for Unit 1 are now complete. Practice these words for your reading comprehension and vocabulary exam questions! 🙏✨
